newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters say UPS backtracked on key issues.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters say UPS backtracked on key issues.

text.p: The Teamsters Union said Thursday that UPS management negotiators backtracked on key issues in contract talks last night and then refused to return to the table this morning.
In a statement posted on the Teamsters' Web site, the union said it would begin a strike against the company at midnight tonight unless the situation changes.
"Teamster members at UPS have already voted to authorize a strike if necessary to get a fair agreement," the statement said.
"The Teamsters negotiating committee continues to be available to meet with the company at any time today and tonight, with or without the presence of a federal mediator," the statement said.

The union said UPS presented it "with recycled proposals that would make the problems UPS members are trying to solve worse instead of better." The Teamsters said the current contract covers more than 185,000 members at UPS nationwide.

The union said UPS management "has refused to agree to real solutions" in areas that are priorities for Teamster members, including "more full-time job opportunities, better Teamster pensions, strong language on subcontracting to keep new job opportunities in-house, and increased job safety and health protection.
